notes.decision: The header preserves only the chapter-marker word; no number or title follows in the visible text. The page begins mid-discourse on the King-of-Darkness's body, suggesting the chapter title and possibly the opening lines were on the previous page or in the lost portion.
ⲧⲃ̄ⲧ = 'fish' (cf. accumulated vocab). The page opens with the fish-likeness — the swimming-creature mode that corresponds to the world of waters in the Manichaean five-fold dark cosmos.

Recurring lexeme (lines 12, 15, 19, 27): creatures with hands, feet, teeth, and tusks who stand before the cosmic being. Etymology unclear; tentatively 'his beasts' on the basis that they are toothed-and-tusked subordinates assembling at his feet. Could alternatively be 'his hosts' or 'his swallowers' (cf. ⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'jaw, swallow'). Flagged for proposed-terms.

Recurring lexeme (lines 14, 17). Likely Greek-derived: either μυριάδες 'myriads' (his innumerable hosts) or μέρη 'parts/members' (his body-limbs). Translated 'myriads' on the basis that the King addresses, hides from, and reveals himself to them — relational behaviors fitting subordinates rather than body-parts. Tentative.
Paired with ⲟⲩⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ 'a killing.' Likely a noun of violence/destruction. Tentatively 'destruction' or 'great-blow' from a root in the ϣⲱⲱϥ/ϣⲱⲣ family. Confidence low.
ⲧⲏⲕ qualitative 'firm, fixed, set fast.' The third item in the second triad: his body is impenetrable. ⲍⲱⲥⲧⲉ = ὥστε 'so that' introduces the consequence (lines 19-21).
ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ = Lyc. for ⲛⲁϫϩⲉ 'teeth' (with ⲍ for ϫ standard); ⲓ̈ⲉⲃⲉ = ⲉⲓⲃϩⲉ 'tusks/molars' or 'fangs.' The pair denotes the dental armament of his beasts.

Iron and bronze (cf. accumulated ⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ, ⲡⲍⲁⲙⲧ̄). ⲥⲉⲛⲁϣϣⲉ = 'cut' (negated ⲉⲛ following). The metals-cannot-pierce-his-body trope echoes K.78 register where the King of Darkness's body is invulnerable to common weapons.

Hyle (ὕλη, Greek 'matter') as the maternal cosmic principle whose 'reflection of single-mindedness' fashions this being. The King of Darkness is here her offspring along with demons and giants — standard Manichaean cosmogonic scheme.
Translated 'giants' as the conventional second member of the Manichaean 'demons and giants' pair (the offspring of Hyle). Possibly an abbreviation or Lycopolitan plural form. Confidence moderate.
Tentatively 'lightning' — paired with ⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' as a phenomenon of the body. Possibly related to ⲙⲡⲉ/ⲉⲃⲣⲏϭⲉ 'thunder/lightning.' Confidence low.
Greek χιών 'snow.' The simile 'his body becomes cold like snow' contrasts with the preceding 'fire' simile in the third triad of attributes.

ⲙⲟⲩⲍ ⲛⲥⲱⲩ idiomatically 'follow after / search out (someone)'; ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲙⲉ tentatively read as ϩⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲙⲉ 'in truth' or as a bridging form to ⲙ̄ⲙⲉ 'to know' on next line. Translated 'searches them out in truth' to capture the sense of penetrative investigation that culminates in 'until he knows what is in their heart.'

ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲁⲩ likely from ⲧⲟⲩⲟ 'show, declare, hand-over' with reflexive object: 'they yield/give themselves to him.' The contrast with the preceding 'standing before him' is between submission/withdrawal vs. assembled presence.

'His life IS the bile (χολή) of [wrath]' — direct correspondential identity in the Manichaean register: the King of Darkness's life-principle = bitter wrath. Not metaphor but ontological identification.
ⲍⲡ̄ⲧⲉ = ϩⲏⲡⲧⲉ/ϩⲏⲡⲉ 'belly, womb, navel.' The body-mapping continues into his belly's contents — but the line breaks before the contents are named.
